title: O David's Son, and David's Lord
description: O David's Son, and David's Lord in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 20, “David's charge to Solomon. 1Chr 28:9”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Da-vid's Son, and Da-vid's Lord! From age to age thou art the same; Thy gra-cious pre-sence now af-ford, And teach our youth to know thy name!

lines: O David's Son, and David's Lord!
From age to age thou art the same;
Thy gracious presence now afford,
And teach our youth to know thy name!
Thy people, Lord, though oft distressed,
Upheld by thee, thus far are come;
And now we long to see thy rest,
And wait thy word to call us home.
Like David, when this life shall end,
We trust in thee sure peace to find;
Like him, to thee we now commend
The children we must leave behind.
Ere long, we hope to be, where care,
And sin, and sorrow, never come
But O! accept our humble prayer,
That these may praise thee in our room.
Show them how vile they are by sin,
And wash them in thy cleansing blood;
O, make them willing to be thine,
And be, to them, a cov'nant God.
Long may thy light and truth remain
To bless this place, when we are gone;
And numbers here be born again,
To dwell for ever near thy throne.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
